categorical_rule: smallest category whose cumulative theta exceeds u; refuse if any u is within 1e-10 of an internal cumulative boundary; no jitter, redraw or clipping
completion: leave every observed raw response byte-value unchanged; inverse-CDF draw keyed 1..5 for each missing cell; convert keyed st4 back to raw 6-keyed; full five-item mean for every invitee
diagnostic: on complete-score respondents, center each keyed item by its complete-score subgroup mean, pool cross-products across the four frame groups; report each of ten within-group residual correlations; flag max absolute correlation > .10 (predeclared teaching flag, not a test). Selection into complete scores can also contribute; diagnostic cannot distinguish model from response-assumption failure.
display: means/bounds 5 decimals; SD/MCSE 6 decimals; counts integer; all numerical CSVs 17 significant digits
draws: independent Gamma(alpha_gjk,scale=1) quantiles of declared uniform primitives, normalized across five categories; one theta per group/item shared by all its missing cells within a completion
failures: empty frame group or no observed answers for a group/item
invalid gamma, simplex or categorical-boundary ambiguity
gamma_numeric: scalar lower incomplete-gamma series/upper continued fraction with 2000-iteration ceiling and 2e-15 convergence, quantile bisection; NumPy 384-node Gauss-Legendre density integration and vector bisection; base R qgamma; fail on invalid or nonconvergent values
group_definition: part_time then first_gen, both completely observed frame variables
identification: joint missingness pattern ignorable for item values conditional only on these two frame variables, with distinct response parameters; conditional independence and exchangeability are additional restrictions, not consequences of MAR
likelihood: within each frame group and item, observed keyed responses are iid categorical with probabilities theta_gj; item responses independent across items conditional on group and theta; item/group probability vectors independent a priori
monte_carlo: Q per completion, Qbar, sample variance B with m-1; estimated MCSE sqrt(B/m) and exact-model MCSE sqrt(analytic_variance/m); compare to analytic model moments without a stochastic pass/fail closeness test
no_missing: bypass primitives and completions; finite target mean equals observed census value, posterior variance and all MC measures zero; no synthetic repeated copies
posterior: alpha_gjk = observed keyed count + 1; independent Dirichlet(alpha_gj) across group/item
posterior_bound: Chebyshev conditional posterior probability at least .95 on [mean-sqrt(variance/.05),mean+sqrt(variance/.05)], intersected with the observed-data support bounds. Conservative, not central 95%, not a frequentist coverage guarantee.
posterior_moments: for cell group/item: A=sum(alpha), mu=sum(k*alpha_k)/A, v=sum(k*k*alpha_k)/A-mu^2, m=number missing; E(sum_missing)=m*mu, Var(sum_missing)=m*(A+m)*v/(A+1). Sum independent cells and divide mean by 5N and variance by (5N)^2. Observed keyed total fixed.
prior: independent Dirichlet(1,1,1,1,1) for each group/item; total prior concentration 5, prior mean score 3
scope_exclusions: claim conditional item independence is plausible in Tonmick
target: finite-roster full keyed five-item stress mean, all 1600 invitees, equal-person weighting
uncertainty: model-conditional finite-roster posterior variance, not a superpopulation sampling SE. Complete-data target variance is zero once all target cells are known. Do not attach the regression pilot U or its t interval.
uniform_order: imputation 1..20; posterior role keys group/item/category in sorted group, st1..st5, 1..5 order; then cell role student_id/item for all originally missing cells, student-ID/item order
variance_parts: expected conditional residual variance = m*A*v/(A+1); shared parameter component = m*m*v/(A+1); add before dividing by (5N)^2
worked_example_selection: first baseline respondent in lexicographic student_id order with any blank stress item
